identity.name: Kingdom of Galicia
alt_names: Kingdom of Galicia and Portugal (García II's title from 1071)

land.text: Galicia, the share of Ordoño II when Alfonso III's lands were partitioned in 910

predecessors.note: The Kingdom of Galicia page: 'Preceded by the Kingdom of Asturias'; 'forced by his sons to abdicate in 910, his lands were partitioned'.

land.text: Galicia, joined to León-Castile when Alfonso VII was crowned in León on 10 March 1126

successors.note: Cliopatria's last Galicia year is 1125. The page's infobox also names the Kingdom of Spain, the County of Portugal and Couto Misto as successors of the long-lived title (to 1833); only the 1126 merger with León is drawn here. The sub-kingdom is a separate polity only in the spells the ledger lists.

capitals.name: Lugo
capitals.note: Ordoño II 'was now recognized as king in an assembly of magnates held in Lugo'; the capital footnote names Lugo and Braga before Compostela and gives no years.

capitals.name: Santiago de Compostela
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Santiago de Compostela; 'Compostela became the capital in the 11th century' (no year given). Alfonso Raimúndez was crowned there in 1111 (Alfonso VII page).

rulers.name: Ordoño II
rulers.title: king of Galicia (also king of León from 914)
rulers.note: Infobox 'Ordoño II (910–924, first)'; the page: 'At the death of García in 914, Ordoño also acquired León'.

rulers.name: Bermudo III
rulers.title: king of León, in refuge in Galicia
rulers.note: Chased from León in 1034 ('retreated into Galicia'); 'After Sancho's death, Bermudo III was immediately received back into León' (1035); killed at Tamarón on 4 September 1037 as king of León. (Reviewer eu-12-c, 2026-10-25: span was 1034-1037)

rulers.name: García II
rulers.title: king of Galicia (and Portugal)
rulers.note: Received Galicia in the 1065 division; invaded in 1071; imprisoned in February 1073; died in or about 1090.

rulers.name: Alfonso VII (Alfonso Raimúndez)
rulers.title: king of Galicia under his mother Urraca
rulers.note: Crowned and anointed at Compostela in 1111; crowned in León on 10 March 1126.

correction.text: the shape as drawn (Galicia with the Bierzo), for 910-914 only; from 914 the crown of Galicia is joined to León's under Ordoño II

keyframe_review.note: 911-921, 46,161 km2 (163 cells: Santiago, Lugo, Ourense, Tui, A Coruña, Ponferrada). The page: Ordoño II received Galicia in the 910 partition and 'At the death of García in 914, Ordoño also acquired León', so the Galician crown is separate only 910-914 (the shape begins a year after the 910 foundation). The infobox gives no area, so the figure cannot be checked. Cliopatria draws León apart to 921 with a 59,553 km2 shape that reaches Braga, Porto and Coimbra; the County of Portugal page calls the county a vassalage of León 'and, during brief periods of division, the Kingdom of Galicia'.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, for 1034-1035 only (Bermudo III's refuge in Galicia until he was received back into León after Sancho III's death in 1035)

keyframe_review.note: 1034-1039, 46,161 km2 (the 911 outline). 'In 1034 he was chased from his throne by King Sancho III of Pamplona and forced to take refuge in Galicia'; Bermudo III 'was killed at the Battle of Tamarón on 4 September 1037' and Ferdinand 'was anointed king in the royal city on 22 June 1038'. The Galicia page: 'In 1037, Bermudo was killed, and Galicia passed with the Kingdom of León into the hands of Ferdinand.' The Bermudo III page: 'After Sancho's death, Bermudo III was immediately received back into León' (Sancho died in 1035). So the separate Galicia holds 1034-1035; from 1035 Galicia is part of Bermudo's León again and passes with it to Ferdinand in 1037. (Reviewer eu-12-c, 2026-10-25: the note said the page was silent on the return; the spell was 1034-1037) Cliopatria has no León shape for 1034-1039.

correction.text: the shape as drawn (Galicia and Portugal south to the Mondego, with Badajoz paying parias), holding 1065-1071

keyframe_review.note: 1066-1071, 90,286 km2 (323 cells: Galicia and Portugal as far as Coimbra, Viseu, Porto). García II's 1065 realm 'extended south to the Mondego River in Portugal with the parias of the Taifa of Badajoz'; Cliopatria's bbox reaches 39.58 N, some 60 km south of the Mondego's mouth, which is within the precision of the century. The page starts the reign in the 1065 division (Cliopatria in 1066) and ends it in 1071; the infobox has no area.

correction.text: Galicia proper (the 911 outline) for 1111-1125, without the Portuguese counties that the 1111 shape adds as far as the Mondego

keyframe_review.note: 1111-1125, 90,216 km2: the 1066 outline repeated, 323 cells reaching Coimbra, Viseu and Porto. The County of Portugal page: Alfonso VI 'in 1096 [...] separate[d] Portugal and Coimbra from Galicia and grant[ed] them to another son-in-law' (Henry, count 1096-1112, then Teresa); Portugal became de facto independent in 1128 (Alfonso VII page). So in 1111-1125 the Galician crown of Alfonso Raimúndez (crowned 1111) covers Galicia proper and not the Portuguese counties; the shape over-reaches by the whole County of Portugal. Neither page describes his territory in words, so the 911 outline stands in.

region.text: Galicia, the share of Ordoño II in the 910 partition, with the assembly of magnates at Lugo

ledger.note: 910: Ordoño II becomes king of Galicia. Infobox 'Established: 910'; 'forced by his sons to abdicate in 910, his lands were partitioned'; Ordoño II received Galicia and 'was now recognized as king in an assembly of magnates held in Lugo.' Cliopatria starts the shape in 911.

region.text: Galicia, joined to León under Ordoño II

ledger.note: 914: Ordoño II adds León to Galicia and the two crowns are joined. 'At the death of García in 914, Ordoño also acquired León'; the page adds that in 924 Fruela 'reunited the realm'. Cliopatria keeps a separate Galicia shape to 921; the León dossier records the same event as a gain of Galicia in 914.

1034: Bermudo III, driven from León by Sancho III of Pamplona, falls back on Galicia. 'In 1034, Sancho wrested the city of León itself from his son-in-law, Bermudo, who retreated into Galicia.' The page does not say how much of Galicia he held; the León dossier has no matching loss for 1034 (it has gaps in Cliopatria for 1034-1039).

region.text: Galicia, passing with León to Ferdinand

ledger.note: 1035: Sancho III dies and Bermudo III is received back into León, so Galicia is again part of his Kingdom of León; it passes with León to Ferdinand I when Bermudo is killed on 4 September 1037. 'By the time Sancho died in 1035, the meseta north of the Duero was dominated by the Pyrenean pocket kingdom of Navarre.' 'After Sancho's death, Bermudo III was immediately received back into León'; 'Bermudo III was killed at the Battle of Tamarón on 4 September 1037.' The Galicia page: 'in 1037, the Castilian count killed Bermudo in battle' and Galicia 'passed with the Kingdom of León into the hands of Ferdinand'. The year is the year of Sancho's death; the page gives no month. (Reviewer eu-12-c, 2026-10-25: was a 1037 merge into kingdom-of-castile at confidence 3; the Bermudo III page puts his return to León immediately after Sancho's death in 1035)

region.text: the County of Galicia 'extended south to the Mondego River in Portugal'

ledger.note: 1065: Ferdinand I's realm is divided and García II receives Galicia. 'In the 1065 division of his father's estates, García was given the County of Galicia'; the realm 'extended south to the Mondego River in Portugal with the parias of the Taifa of Badajoz'. The Galicia page: 'In 1063, Ferdinand chose to partition his realm; he died in 1065.' Cliopatria starts the shape in 1066 and draws Ferdinand's undivided realm in its Castile row to 1065.

region.text: the Taifa of Badajoz, tributary through its parias

ledger.note: 1065: the Taifa of Badajoz pays parias to the king of Galicia. The 1065 division gave García a realm 'with the parias of the Taifa of Badajoz'; the page says only that Badajoz paid tribute and names no ruler.

region.text: Galicia and northern Portugal, invaded by Alfonso VI

ledger.note: 1071: Alfonso VI invades Galicia and García's kingdom ends. 'in May or early June 1071, he invaded Galicia and northern Portugal'; 'Sancho likely acquiesced in this in exchange for partial control over the realm'; García was defeated near Santarém, held briefly in Castile and allowed to flee to Seville, and 'García's independent kingdom of Galicia and Portugal ceased to exist.' The page does not date the end more closely than 1071-1072 and does not say how Alfonso and Sancho shared the land; Cliopatria draws the combined realm of 1072 in its Castile row.

region.text: the Taifa of Badajoz, no longer tributary to Galicia

ledger.note: 1071: the parias of Badajoz end with the kingdom. The page names the tribute only in the 1065 division and says nothing of its end; the year bridges the fall of the kingdom.

region.text: Galicia proper, the kingdom of Alfonso Raimúndez

ledger.note: 1111: Alfonso Raimúndez is crowned king of Galicia at Compostela. He 'became the King of Galicia in 1111'; 'In 1111, Diego Gelmírez, Bishop of Compostela and the count of Traba, crowned and anointed' him. Portugal and Coimbra had been separated from Galicia in 1096 (County of Portugal page), so the land is Galicia proper. (Reviewer eu-12-c, 2026-10-25: counterpart was kingdom-of-leon; in the sibling dossiers León holds no land 1072-1126 (kingdom-of-leon loses its land to kingdom-of-castile in 1072 and regains it in 1126) and kingdom-of-castile records the 1111 loss of Galicia)

1126: Alfonso VII is crowned in León and Galicia is joined to his kingdom. 'On 10 March 1126, after the death of his mother, he was crowned in León.' Cliopatria's last Galicia year is 1125; the León dossier records the gain of Galicia in 1126.

1126: the separate kingdom of Galicia ends when Alfonso VII, king of Galicia since 1111, becomes sole ruler on 10 March 1126. The Kingdom of Galicia page lists a title that lasted to 1833 (infobox 'Dissolved: 1833'), but after 1126 Galicia is drawn inside León-Castile.

wars.name: Capture of León by Sancho III of Pamplona (1034)
wars.outcome: Sancho III took the city of León and Bermudo III retreated into Galicia; 'By the time Sancho died in 1035, the meseta north of the Duero was dominated by the Pyrenean pocket kingdom of Navarre.'
wars.note: Named from the Bermudo III page; no separate article was opened. The zone is Leonese, not Galician; the Galician consequence is the 1034 refuge.

wars.name: Alfonso VI's invasion of Galicia and northern Portugal (1071)

zones.text: Galicia and northern Portugal, invaded in 'May or early June 1071'

wars.outcome: García II lost his kingdom; Sancho II defeated him in central Portugal, he fled to Seville, and in October 1072 Sancho was assassinated at Zamora, after which Alfonso 'seiz[ed] Sancho's reunited realm'.
wars.note: No Wikipedia article of this name was opened; named from the García II page. The page does not say who held which part of Galicia in 1071-1072.

certainty.note: Frontiers are those of an early medieval kingdom, given by rivers (the Mondego in 1065-1071) and by the pages' words; none is a treaty or survey line. The southern limit moves with the County of Portugal (separated in 1096).

notes: Cliopatria's four shapes (911-921, 1034-1039, 1066-1071, 1111-1125) are the spells when Galicia was drawn as a kingdom of its own; the pages date more. Reviewed: 911-921 holds only 910-914 (merged with León 914); 1034-1039 holds 1034-1035 (Bermudo III was received back into León after Sancho III's death in 1035; reviewer eu-12-c); 1066-1071 holds 1065-1071; 1111-1125 over-reaches into the County of Portugal (separated 1096). Sub-kings not drawn because the page gives no extent or end: Ordoño IV 'enthroned in Santiago de Compostela in 958' until Sancho 'reclaimed the crown in 960'; Bermudo II crowned at Santiago in 982 (no end date on the page); Fruela's reunion in 924. The Kingdom of Galicia page's infobox says 1833, its text 1834; the Ferdinand II death year is 1188 in the text and 1187 on a caption; the page (Galicia) says García 'went into exile in 1072 and returned in 1073' while the García II page has him taken prisoner in February 1073: the dossier uses the García II page. The Alfonso VII page and the Galicia page give no area for any period, so no Cliopatria area could be compared with an infobox. Counterparts: 'kingdom-of-castile' stands for Ferdinand I's undivided realm (Cliopatria's Castile row 1046-1065) and for the combined realm of 1072; 'kingdom-of-leon' for the León crown in 914, 1034, 1035 and 1126; 'kingdom-of-castile' also for 1111, when the sibling dossiers hold León inside Castile (1072-1126) (reviewer eu-12-c). The León dossier has gains of Galicia in 914 and 1126 only; the 1034 and 1035 moves have no matching event there (the 1065, 1071 and 1111 moves are matched in kingdom-of-castile). Region names: all resolve (Galicia (Spain), Cliopatria shapes); no gazetteer name is missing.
